dialogues.title: Visitando um apartamento
dialogues.context: Diego wants to rent an apartment. The real estate agent, Helena, shows it to him.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Bom dia, Diego! Este é o apartamento.
lines.en: Good morning, Diego! This is the apartment.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Que apartamento claro! Quantos quartos tem?
lines.en: What a bright apartment! How many bedrooms does it have?

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Tem dois quartos, uma sala, uma cozinha e um banheiro.
lines.en: It has two bedrooms, a living room, a kitchen and a bathroom.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Tem varanda?
lines.en: Is there a balcony?

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Tem, sim. A varanda é pequena, mas é bonita.
lines.en: Yes, there is. The balcony is small, but it is pretty.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: E garagem? Tem garagem no prédio?
lines.en: And a garage? Does the building have a garage?

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Tem, sim. O condomínio custa trezentos reais.
lines.en: Yes, it does. The condomínio fee costs three hundred reais.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: E o aluguel? Quanto é?
lines.en: And the rent? How much is it?

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: O aluguel é dois mil reais.
lines.en: The rent is two thousand reais.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Em que andar fica o apartamento?
lines.en: On which floor is the apartment?

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: No quinto andar. Tem elevador.
lines.en: On the fifth floor. There is an elevator.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: É barulhento?
lines.en: Is it noisy?

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.pt: Não, é muito tranquilo.
lines.en: No, it is very quiet.

dialogues.title: Na casa da Juliana
dialogues.context: Juliana invites her friend Paulo to her house for the first time.

lines.speaker: Juliana
lines.pt: Entra, Paulo! Essa é a minha casa.
lines.en: Come in, Paulo! This is my house.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.pt: Que legal! A sala é bem grande.
lines.en: How nice! The living room is really big.

lines.speaker: Juliana
lines.pt: É, mas o resto da casa é pequeno.
lines.en: Yes, but the rest of the house is small.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.pt: Onde fica o banheiro?
lines.en: Where is the bathroom?

lines.speaker: Juliana
lines.pt: Fica ao lado da cozinha.
lines.en: It is next to the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.pt: Você tem quintal?
lines.en: Do you have a backyard?

lines.speaker: Juliana
lines.pt: Tenho, atrás da casa. Tem uma mesa e quatro cadeiras.
lines.en: I do, behind the house. There is a table and four chairs.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.pt: E a geladeira? Está na cozinha?
lines.en: And the refrigerator? Is it in the kitchen?

lines.speaker: Juliana
lines.pt: Está, ao lado do fogão. Tem suco lá dentro.
lines.en: Yes, next to the stove. There is juice in there.

lines.speaker: Paulo
lines.pt: Ótimo! Eu quero um suco.
lines.en: Great! I want a juice.

dialogues.title: Conhecendo o bairro
dialogues.context: Lucas has just moved into a new building. He asks his neighbor, Dona Marta, about the neighborhood.

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.pt: Bom dia, Dona Marta! Eu sou o Lucas, o novo vizinho.
lines.en: Good morning, Dona Marta! I'm Lucas, the new neighbor.

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.pt: Prazer, Lucas! Bem-vindo ao prédio.
lines.en: Nice to meet you, Lucas! Welcome to the building.

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.pt: Obrigado. Tem mercado aqui perto?
lines.en: Thank you. Is there a supermarket near here?

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.pt: Tem, sim. Tem um mercado e uma padaria na esquina.
lines.en: Yes, there is. There's a supermarket and a bakery on the corner.

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.pt: O bairro é tranquilo?
lines.en: Is the neighborhood quiet?

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.pt: É, mas à noite tem um pouco de barulho na rua.
lines.en: It is, but at night there is a little noise in the street.

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.pt: E tem ônibus?
lines.en: And are there buses?

lines.speaker: Marta
lines.pt: Tem bastante ônibus. O ponto fica em frente ao prédio.
lines.en: There are plenty of buses. The stop is across from the building.

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.pt: Perfeito! Muito obrigado, Dona Marta.
lines.en: Perfect! Thank you very much, Dona Marta.

grammar.title: Tem and há: saying what exists
grammar.explanation:
To say that something exists in a place, Brazilians use tem, which is the third person singular of ter. In this meaning it never changes: tem um sofá, tem dois quartos, tem muitas janelas. It does not matter if what exists is singular or plural, or whether it is a person or a thing.

The formal equivalent is há (from haver). You will see it in writing, on signs and in formal speech: há vagas, há dois quartos. In everyday conversation tem is much more common. Both are used in questions and negative sentences in the same way: tem varanda? não tem elevador. In speech you can drop the subject and the place can go at the start or the end: tem um banco aqui, or aqui tem um banco.

Do not confuse this tem with ter meaning to own. Eu tenho um apartamento says that I own one, and o apartamento tem dois quartos says that it contains two. The plural têm, with an accent, belongs to ter with a plural subject: eles têm dois filhos. The existential tem never takes an accent.

grammar.title: Muito, pouco, bastante, tanto
grammar.explanation:
These four words express quantity and they behave in two ways. Before a noun they are adjectives and agree with it: muito barulho, muita luz, muitos quartos, muitas janelas. Pouco works the same way: pouco espaço, poucas janelas. Tanto also agrees: tanto barulho, tanta gente. Bastante means quite a lot or plenty. It stays bastante before a singular noun, and before a plural noun you can use bastante in speech or bastantes in careful writing: bastante espaço, bastantes janelas.

Before an adjective or another adverb they are adverbs and never change: a casa é muito grande, a sala é pouco clara, o bairro é bastante tranquilo, a rua é tão barulhenta. Before an adjective, tanto becomes tão: tão grande, tão caro. Bastante is a little weaker than muito and means fairly or quite.

Pouco before an adjective gives the sense of not very: o quarto é pouco claro means the bedroom is not very bright. In speech people more often say não é muito claro.

grammar.title: Estar and ficar for location
grammar.explanation:
Both estar and ficar say where something is. Ficar is normal for things that stay in one place, such as buildings, streets, cities and rooms: a cozinha fica ao lado da sala, o banco fica na esquina. Estar is used for things that can move, or for the exact position of an object right now: o sofá está na sala, as chaves estão em cima da mesa, o Pedro está em casa.

In speech, people use both for furniture without much difference, so o sofá fica na sala and o sofá está na sala are both heard. When you ask where a place is, onde fica...? is the natural choice, and onde é...? is also common. For a person or a moving object, ask onde está...? Onde está o Pedro?

Use the prepositions from the last unit to be precise: em cima de (on top of), embaixo de (under), dentro de (inside), fora de (outside), perto de, ao lado de, entre. They contract with the article: em cima da mesa, embaixo da cama, dentro do armário.

grammar.title: Describing places
grammar.explanation:
Use ser to describe the lasting characteristics of a home or a neighborhood: a casa é grande, o apartamento é pequeno, o bairro é tranquilo. Use estar for temporary conditions: hoje a rua está barulhenta, a sala está escura. Adjectives come after the noun and agree with it: uma sala grande, um quarto pequeno, uma rua barulhenta, apartamentos claros.

Useful adjectives for places are grande, pequeno, claro (bright) and escuro (dark), barulhento (noisy), tranquilo (quiet), bonito, feio, novo and velho. Adjectives ending in -e or -l, such as grande and azul, have the same form for masculine and feminine. Adjectives ending in -o change to -a: claro, clara; barulhento, barulhenta.

Use muito, pouco or bastante before the adjective to adjust it: muito claro, bastante tranquilo, pouco barulhento. Join two ideas with mas (but): a casa é pequena, mas é muito clara.

culture.title: Casas, apartamentos and condomínios
culture.text:
Most people in large Brazilian cities live in an apartamento in a prédio, often with a porteiro who controls the entrance all day. People in smaller towns and suburbs more often live in a casa with a quintal. Many apartments have a small varanda with a churrasqueira, a grill for the weekend barbecue, and most homes have an área de serviço, a small space next to the kitchen with the washing machine.

When you rent, you usually pay two amounts each month: the aluguel to the owner and the condomínio to the building, which covers shared costs such as the porteiro, cleaning and the elevator. There may also be an annual property tax called IPTU. Renting usually requires a fiador, a guarantor, or a security deposit. The person who manages the building is the síndico, and residents meet in an assembleia.

A kitchenette apartment is called a quitinete, and a very small apartment is often called an apê in casual speech. Floors are counted from the térreo, the ground floor, so the primeiro andar is the first floor above it. In many buildings the elevator buttons show T for térreo and sometimes G for garagem.
